videos.title: If I Owned a Home Service Business in 2026, This Is Where I'd Put AI
videos.formula: If I Started [Topic] in [Year], This Is What I Would Do (1.0M views a month, title-structures.md)
alt_titles: Stop Using AI Everywhere. Put It Here Instead.
The Real Reason AI Isn't Making You Money Yet
videos.research: #7 "How can AI help a business like mine?"
videos.why: The biggest search cluster in the research: Google #1 with 158 organic searches like "how can i use ai for my hvac business", plus 55 more for "what can ai do for my business", YouTube autocomplete, and 22 Reddit "what are you actually using AI for" posts. Every owner asks it and no owner channel draws the answer.
videos.hook: Everyone tells you to use AI everywhere. Don't. Put it where your money leaks.

beats.t: LEADS: leads come in every day: calls, forms, texts
The pipe: your business turns leads into paid jobs. That's all it does
LEAKS: money drips out in three places: the call nobody answers, the quote nobody follows up, the lead that comes in after hours
Plug the leaks: AI goes on the leaks, biggest first. Not on writing your Instagram captions
PAID: the same leads, more paid jobs at the end. No new ad spend

videos.close: Start with the first leak, the phone. Our AI demo is that first plug, trained on your own website. Link below.
videos.reel_headline: Don't use AI everywhere. Plug the leaks.
videos.reel_idea: Draw the pipe, the three drips, then the three plugs. One line per leak.

draw.what: "LEADS" on the left with three arrows pointing right
A long pipe across the middle (two lines, open ends)
Drips under the pipe in three spots, a phone, a paper and a moon under them, "LEAKS" under the middle one
A small plug on each leak
An arrow out of the right end to a big $, "PAID" under it

videos.title: What Actually Happens When Owners Throw Their Worst Calls at an AI
videos.formula: What Actually Happens When You [Action] (863K views a month, title-structures.md)
alt_titles: Owners Threw Nearly 500 Nightmare Calls at Our AI
Can AI Handle Your Hardest Calls? Owners Tested It
videos.research: #14 "Can it handle my calls? Mine are complicated."
videos.why: About 570 data points, mostly his own: across all demo tenants, owners threw emergencies and after hours calls at the demo in 368 sessions, angry complaints in 43 and off topic trick questions in 57 ("will it rain today in dallas", "What model are you trained on?"). A radio host trying to break an AI receptionist got 85k views. Nobody else has this data.
videos.hook: When owners test our AI, they don't ask nice questions. They throw their worst calls at it.

beats.t: The AI is your business on the phone
EMERGENCY: "water everywhere, it's 9 pm". A good AI hears it's urgent, gets the address and gets it to you now (368 emergency and after hours tests, our own demo data)
ANGRY: a customer yelling about a bad job. A good AI stays calm, never argues, never promises a refund, takes the note and hands it to you (43 tests)
WEIRD: "will it rain today in Dallas?", "what model are you?". A good AI answers in one line and steers back to booking (57 tests)
The checks: three different calls, one rule. It knows what it is allowed to do and when to hand off

videos.close: Your turn. Throw your worst call at our demo, link below, and grade it yourself.
videos.reel_headline: Owners threw their worst calls at our AI
videos.reel_idea: Three bolts, three checks, one line each on what a good AI does.

draw.what: A box with a phone handset inside, middle of the board (the AI)
"EMERGENCY" top left, a lightning bolt into the box, then a green arrow and check on the right
"ANGRY" middle left, a bolt into the box, then its green check
"WEIRD" bottom left, a bolt into the box, then its green check
Point at the three checks

notes: The counts are keyword match counts across all demo tenants, so say "about" and "our own demo data". We have counts of tests, not pass rates: teach what a good answer looks like, do not claim it aced all of them.

videos.title: The Honest Truth About AI and Your Front Desk
videos.formula: The [Adjective] Truth About [Topic] (4.8M views a month, title-structures.md)
alt_titles: Watch This Before You Tell Your Staff About AI
What Everyone Gets Wrong About AI and Front Desk Jobs
videos.research: #8 "Will AI replace my front desk? What do I tell my staff?"
videos.why: The biggest theme in the comments of business AI videos (on a video about an owner who replaced 7 employees, the top doubts were "what happens when he's sick" and "who does the work"). Google: 44 searches, including People Also Ask "Will receptionists be replaced by AI?". 7 owners raised it on our own demo: "half my team is resistant to AI... they think it'll take their job".
videos.hook: An owner told our demo: half my team is afraid AI will take their job. Here's what I'd tell them.

beats.t: Your front desk person
PHONES: job one is the phones, ringing all day: hours, prices, "can you come Tuesday"
PEOPLE: job two is the person standing right in front of them. Today those two jobs fight, so somebody always waits
Move only the phone lane to AI: the repeat calls, after hours and overflow
Your person turns to the customer in the room. That's the part AI can't do
What to tell your staff: it takes the calls you hate, not your job. Let them pick which calls go first

videos.close: Have your front desk call our demo, link below. They'll tell you which calls they'd happily hand off.
videos.reel_headline: AI should take the phones, not the person.
videos.reel_idea: Desk, ringing phones, the customer waiting, the arrow to AI, the heart.

draw.what: A stick figure behind a desk, left half
Three ringing phones above its head, "PHONES" above them
A customer stick figure facing the desk, "PEOPLE" above its head
A box with a handset, top right, and a curved arrow from the phones into it
A small heart between the desk person and the customer
draw.during: Turns to the customer, what to tell staff

notes: Do not promise nobody gets let go; that is each owner's call. The frame is phones versus people.

videos.title: Watch This Before You Buy AI From Anyone
videos.formula: Watch This Before [Action] (1.0M views a month, title-structures.md)
alt_titles: Is That AI Agency a Scam? Ask These 3 Questions
3 Questions That Expose a Bad AI Vendor
videos.research: #11 "Everyone is pitching me AI. How do I tell who's legit?"
videos.why: Owners are drowning in AI pitches: 50,307 AI agency cold emails from member inboxes got 83 replies, mostly auto replies, and the human ones said "Not clear what you do. Not clear what you deliver." (our own data). 13 Reddit posts fed up with AI pitches. The August study: support that vanishes after payment (22) and vendor doubts (26). Nobody hands owners a simple filter.
videos.hook: Every week someone pitches you AI. Three questions sort the real ones from the rest.

beats.t: The inbox: AI pitches every day. One owner's real reply: "Not clear what you do. Not clear what you deliver."
PROOF?: "Show me on MY business, live." Not a slide deck, not someone else's case study
WHO FIXES?: "When it says something wrong at 9 pm on a Saturday, who fixes it, and how fast?" Support that vanishes after payment is a top complaint from owners who bought
EXIT?: "If I leave, do I keep my phone number and my data? Is there a contract?"
The check: whoever passes all three gets a call back. Everyone else, delete

videos.close: The proof test is a live demo on your own business, not a slide deck. Here's ours, link below. Ask us all three first.
videos.reel_headline: 3 questions before you buy AI from anyone
videos.reel_idea: Inbox, funnel, the three questions fast, one check.

draw.what: An inbox tray overflowing with envelopes, upper left
A funnel in the middle with an arrow from the tray, "PROOF?" on its right
"WHO FIXES?" under it, pointing at the funnel
"EXIT?" under that
An arrow down from the spout to one big check

notes: Quote the reply as "a real reply an owner sent an AI agency"; do not say on camera where the email numbers come from.

videos.title: You've Been Lied to About AI Replacing the Trades
videos.formula: You've Been Lied to About [Topic] (975K views a month, title-structures.md)
alt_titles: AI Won't Fix Your Furnace. Here's What It Will Do.
The Honest Truth About AI and the Trades
videos.why: Google: 51 searches like "will ai replace plumbers" and "can ai replace hvac technicians". 12 Reddit posts ("Will AI take over plumbing?"). The most discussed owner video in the sample, "AI Will Make Plumbers Earn More Than Lawyers!", has 1.9M views and 7,356 comments; its top comment, "If no one has a job who's gonna pay the plumbers?", has 2,900 likes.
videos.hook: A video about AI and plumbers got 1.9 million views. The top comment: if no one has a job, who's gonna pay the plumbers?

beats.t: Draw a line down the middle: there are two kinds of work in your business
HANDS: diagnosing, fixing, installing, being trusted inside someone's home. AI is not coming for that
PAPERWORK: the phone, the schedule, the invoice, the follow up. That is what AI takes
The arrow back: every hour the paperwork stops eating goes to paid jobs
Who actually loses: not the trade. The shop that lets the phone ring out while the one down the street answers

videos.close: AI won't fix the furnace. It answers the phone about the furnace. Hear it on our demo, link below.
videos.reel_headline: AI won't take your trade. It takes your paperwork.
videos.reel_idea: The line, the wrench, the three icons, the arrow back with the $.

videos.title: What Actually Happens When a Customer Asks ChatGPT for a Plumber
videos.formula: What Actually Happens When You [Action] (863K views a month, title-structures.md)
alt_titles: Your Next Customer Won't Google You
The Customer Shift Nobody Is Talking About
videos.why: 22 Reddit posts on AI search in the last 12 months, about 11 from owners asking, e.g. "My partner and I's firm has practiced for 30 years, and ChatGPT recommends newer firms" and "Anyone had a customer say they found you through ChatGPT instead of Google?". The August study: "Google's AI is calling me asking for prices". A new, fast growing question that no owner channel draws.
videos.hook: Your next customer might not Google you. They'll ask ChatGPT: who's the best plumber near me?

beats.t: BEST PLUMBER?: the customer asks an AI chat instead of scrolling Google
The chat answers with a short list: two or three shops, not ten pages. It builds the list from what's out there about you: your site, your reviews, your listings
WHO ANSWERS?: the customer calls the first name. Getting recommended is half the game. If it rings out, they call number two
The check: the shop that picks up and books wins the job
This week: make your site say plainly what you do, where and when, keep reviews coming, answer every call

videos.close: Getting recommended is half. Answering is the other half. That's what our demo does, link below.
videos.reel_headline: Customers now ask ChatGPT for a plumber. Then what?
videos.reel_idea: The question, the short list, the ringing phone, the one check.

draw.what: A customer with a phone, upper left, speech bubble "BEST PLUMBER?"
A chat window in the middle with an arrow from the bubble, three arrows to three small houses on the right
A ringing phone lower left, "WHO ANSWERS?", an arrow up to the top house
A check next to the top house
draw.during: The check, this week, the close

notes: How the chat picks shops is simplified on purpose ("what's out there about you"); do not promise a ranking trick.
